title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Bootstrap inference provides confidence intervals indirect effects without assuming normality. medfit implements three bootstrap methods: Parametric bootstrap: Sample parameter distribution (fast, assumes normality) Nonparametric bootstrap: Resample data refit models (robust, slower) Plugin estimator: Point estimate (fastest, CI) methods return BootstrapResult object consistent structure.

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: serial mediation (treatment -> mediator1 -> mediator2 -> outcome), indirect effect product chain’s paths, \(\times d \times b\). parametric plugin methods accept SerialMediationData object (ParallelMediationData, InteractionMediationData, JointMediationData) well MediationData. statistic_fn receives named @estimates vector, carries chain’s path aliases , d1, b, c_prime: lm chain estimates equation separately, covariance matrix sets covariances equations zero (see Model Extraction article). avoid assumption, bootstrap nonparametrically resampling data refitting three models:
code: # Fit the chain: each model adjusts for the covariates and every upstream # variable, so the outcome model includes mediator1 as well as mediator2 fit_serial <- function(d) {   extract_mediation(     lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     model_y = lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator2 +                    covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     treatment = "treatment",     mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),     mediator_models = list(       lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)     )   ) } serial_med <- fit_serial(mediation_demo)  # Point estimate of the serial indirect effect (a * d * b) serial_med@a_path * serial_med@d_path * serial_med@b_path [1] 0.07545039 # Parametric bootstrap: draw the chain's paths from N(estimates, vcov) boot_serial_param <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(theta) unname(theta["a"] * theta["d1"] * theta["b"]),   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = serial_med,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial_param) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   parametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0371   Upper:   0.1248 boot_serial <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(boot_data) {     s <- fit_serial(boot_data)     s@a_path * s@d_path * s@b_path   },   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0383   Upper:   0.1187

title: Model Extraction
text: extract_mediation() function provides standardized interface extracting mediation structures fitted models. works : - lm/glm models (base R) - implemented - lavaan SEM models - implemented - lmer mixed models (future) Extraction returns S7 class matches structure: MediationData, InteractionMediationData, SerialMediationData, ParallelMediationData, JointMediationData. share one interface (nie(), confint(), tidy(), bootstrap_mediation(), …) across modeling frameworks. Note: quick analysis, consider using med() instead - handles fitting extraction one step. Use extract_mediation() need control already fitted models.

title: Model Extraction
text: treatment mediator interact, total effect splits four pieces (VanderWeele 2014): controlled direct effect (CDE), reference interaction (INTref), mediated interaction (INTmed), pure indirect effect (PIE), Total = CDE + INTref + INTmed + PIE, NDE = CDE + INTref, NIE = INTmed + PIE. medfit computes decomposition; causal interpretation (requires VanderWeele’s -unmeasured-confounding assumptions) analyst’s responsibility. extract_mediation() returns InteractionMediationData object whenever outcome model carries X:M term. Set reference mediator level m_star (default 0). lm/glm, X:M term detected automatically. mediation_demo’s outcome_int carries treatment mediator1 interaction: tidy() reports four components type = "components" natural effects type = "effects"; glance() adds interaction coefficient m_star: four-way formulas (continuous Y M) CDE = θ₁ + θ₃·m*, INTref = θ₃·(E[M|X=0] − m*), INTmed = θ₃·β₁, PIE = θ₂·β₁, θ₃ interaction coefficient β₁ path. Non-Gaussian outcomes yet supported raise informative error. lavaan interaction enters product variable (column create), model must fit meanstructure = TRUE mediator intercept (needed INTref) estimated. Name product term via interaction: interaction absent (decomposition = "two_way"), extraction falls back standard MediationData — existing two-way workflows unchanged. two paths extract models fit. fit_mediation() can instead delegate fitting regmedint package, implements VanderWeele’s regression-based estimators closed form, hand back medfit classes: return class follows rule extract_mediation(): X:M term formula_y yields InteractionMediationData, absence plain MediationData. Components map regmedint’s output CDE = cde, INTref = pnde − cde, INTmed = tnie − pnie, PIE = pnie. Standard errors come regmedint’s delta method rather medfit’s, analytical — bootstrap needed — reproduce SEs regmedint::summary() reports model. four-way split read reference mediator level \(m^*\): \[\text{CDE} = \theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*\] \[\text{INTref} = \theta_3\,(E[M \mid X = 0] - m^*)\] Set fit_mediation(m_star = ), defaults 0 every engine: two terms shift exactly compensating directions, nde(), nie(), te(), pm() invariant m_star — CDE/INTref split moves. Passing m_star fit treatment--mediator term error, silent -op. engines reach answer different routes. engine = "glm" applies m_star extraction time, coefficients fit; engine = "regmedint" hands value regmedint::regmedint() m_cde argument, closed-form estimator consumes fitting time. two names denote one quantity, m_cde accepted engine_args — use m_star. Everything regmedint-specific reference level goes engine_args: Recognized names interaction, cvar, mreg, yreg, a0, a1, c_cond; replaces value adapter otherwise derive formulas, families, data. Scope. regmedint engine needs numeric 0/1 treatment linear (Gaussian) mediator model; outcome may Gaussian binomial. Outside range regmedint’s closed-form effects stop products regression coefficients MediationData InteractionMediationData defined terms , adapter raises explicit error instead returning object whose numbers disagree nie(). weights se_type = "sandwich" likewise refused rather silently ignored. regmedint suggested package — install install.packages("regmedint").
